description: Isaiah described our culture thousands of years ago. Truth is gone. Anyone who renounces evil is attacked. But God sees it, and He is not done.

verse: "Yes, truth is gone, and anyone who renounces evil is attacked. The Lord looked and was displeased to find there was no justice."
body_html:
This passage sounds exactly like our culture today.

Truth is gone. If you speak the truth in almost any public space right now, you will pay for it. Truth about biology. Truth about morality. Truth about God. Truth about the Bible. Truth about right and wrong. The moment you speak it, someone comes for you.

Anyone who renounces evil is attacked. Read that line again slowly. The people who dare to name what is actually evil and refuse to be part of it are the ones who get labeled as the problem. Not the people doing the evil. The ones speaking against it.

That is exactly where we are.

Christians who hold to biblical truth get called hateful. Parents who protect their kids from what culture wants to push on them get called extremists. Anyone who dares to say a hard word about the direction things are going gets piled on. The moral order has been flipped completely upside down. The wicked are celebrated and the ones renouncing evil are attacked.

And Isaiah is describing this thousands of years ago.

Which means this is not new. It is the same pattern that has played out in every generation when a culture drifts far enough from God. Truth becomes offensive. Righteousness becomes intolerable. Anyone who stands for what is right gets treated like the enemy.

The Lord looked and was displeased to find there was no justice.

He sees it. He is not blind to what is happening. He is not indifferent. He is displeased. That should tell us a lot about how He views the state of our culture. He is not okay with it. He is not shrugging. He is grieved and angered by the injustice, the deception, and the persecution of those who try to walk in truth.

But the verses right after this one are the ones we need to hold onto.

Because Isaiah goes on to say that when God saw no one stepping in to help, He stepped in Himself. He put on righteousness as body armor. He put on the helmet of salvation. He clothed Himself and moved on behalf of His people.

Many read that as pointing straight to Jesus.

When no human being could fix what was broken, God Himself put on flesh and stepped into the mess. He did what no one else could do. He is still the one who sets things right, even now.

So when the world feels like Isaiah 59, and it does, we do not have to spiral. We are not the first generation to watch truth disappear. And God is not sitting still. He sees it. He is at work. And in the end, He is the one who will make everything right.

Our job is to keep standing. To keep speaking truth even when it costs us. To keep renouncing evil even when we get attacked for it. To keep walking with Him even when the culture pulls hard in every other direction.

Because He sees. And He is not done.

Are you willing to stand for truth even when it costs you, and are you trusting that God is still at work even when the world looks like Isaiah 59?
